heroHeadline: New Out-of-Control Fire Doubles Twice Near Sooke, BC as Rest of Canada's Wildfire Season Keeps Fading
heroSubtitle: A newly discovered wildfire on Mount Jack, west of Sooke on southern Vancouver Island, has doubled in size twice since September 20 — from 35 hectares Sunday to 100 hectares Tuesday to 210.4 hectares by Wednesday morning — fuelled by warm, dry and windy conditions, though BC Wildfire Service has issued no evacuation orders or alerts and says it threatens no structures. It is one of five out-of-control fires currently burning on Vancouver Island. Elsewhere, the wind-down continues: BC's season-wide active count has fallen to 105 fires (5 out of control) from 150 three weeks ago, Northwestern Ontario ticked up to 30 active fires after a single new 0.1-hectare start (Thunder Bay 89, Pigeon River Provincial Park) on September 22, and the Northwest Territories' active count has fallen to 79 from 219 in early September. No new deaths or evacuation orders were identified this cycle.
footerNote: Data sourced from official reports, major outlets, and institutional analyses.
